l4_steps.name: Load interline & SPA agreement terms into RA system
l4_steps.input: Signed interline agreement or Special Prorate Agreement (SPA) from commercial team
l4_steps.output: Active prorate factor set and SPA parameters loaded in ARA
l4_steps.kpi: Agreement setup lead time ≤5 business days from signature
l4_steps.pain_point: No standard digital handoff format for SPA terms — analysts manually transcribe flat-rate splits and minimum guarantees into ARA, introducing keying errors that cause systematic mis-proration

l4_steps.name: Ingest ATPCO prorate factor tables (PF Tables)
l4_steps.input: IATA Resolution 850 prorate tables published via ATPCO filing cycle
l4_steps.output: Validated prorate factor file loaded into ARA for IATA-standard interline tickets
l4_steps.kpi: Prorate table update cycle ≤24 hours after ATPCO publication date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO publishes 26 fare filing cycles per year; delayed ingestion causes mis-proration on interline tickets issued in the gap window — revenue impact typically discovered only at quarterly ICH reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Classify ticket as interline, codeshare, or hybrid
l4_steps.input: Issued electronic ticket (ET) with multi-carrier coupon segments and validating carrier code
l4_steps.output: Ticket classified with proration method assigned: IATA standard, SPA override, or codeshare split
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-classification rate ≥95% of interline tickets without manual intervention
l4_steps.pain_point: Codeshare tickets with separate operating vs marketing carrier codes require different proration logic than pure interline; misclassification routes codeshare revenue through ICH instead of bilateral settlement, triggering partner disputes

l4_steps.name: Extract OD fare components and fare basis codes
l4_steps.input: ET record with fare breakdown, applicable fare basis codes, and coupon sequence
l4_steps.output: Per-segment fare basis code, ticketed point mileage (TPM), and applicable fare component isolated per coupon
l4_steps.kpi: Fare extraction error rate <0.5% of processed interline tickets
l4_steps.pain_point: Mixed class of service within a single ticket (e.g., J class on carrier A, Y class on carrier B) complicates fare basis assignment under IATA Resolution 762 — ARA auto-extraction fails on ~8% of mixed-cabin interline itineraries requiring manual override

l4_steps.name: Apply IATA mileage proration to derive carrier percentages
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Prorate Data + Amadeus Revenue Accounting (ARA)
l4_steps.input: Per-segment ticketed point mileage (TPM), total OD fare amount, ATPCO PF tables
l4_steps.output: Carrier-specific proration percentage and prorated revenue amount per segment
l4_steps.kpi: Mileage calculation accuracy ≥99.5% against IATA TACT reference data
l4_steps.pain_point: Mileage discrepancies between IATA TACT mileage tables and GDS-routed itineraries (reroutes, diversions) cause variance — airlines typically absorb or dispute the difference at quarterly ICH reconciliation rather than fixing source data

l4_steps.name: Apply Special Prorate Agreement overrides where eligible
l4_steps.input: SPA terms: flat-rate splits, percentage overrides, minimum/maximum guarantees per route and cabin
l4_steps.output: SPA-adjusted revenue allocation per carrier segment, superseding IATA mileage proration where SPA applies
l4_steps.kpi: SPA override application rate = 100% for all tickets on SPA-covered routes during SPA validity period
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines maintain 50–200+ active SPAs; no automated expiry alerting in ARA means analysts continue applying lapsed SPA terms, generating overpayments recovered only at annual SPA audit — average recovery lag is 14 months

l4_steps.name: Allocate taxes and YQ/YR surcharges per carrier rules
l4_steps.input: Tax and surcharge breakdown from ET record: government taxes, YQ fuel surcharge, YR carrier-imposed surcharge
l4_steps.output: Tax allocation per carrier — carrier-specific government taxes retained by respective carrier; YQ/YR allocated per agreement or IATA Resolution 728
l4_steps.kpi: Tax allocation error rate <0.1% of total ticket value across processed interline tickets
l4_steps.pain_point: YQ/YR fuel surcharge allocation rules vary by bilateral agreement and route — IATA Resolution 728 defaults are frequently overridden in SPAs, and smaller partner carriers often apply inconsistent rules, causing disputed tax remittance averaging $12–18 per ticket

l4_steps.name: Generate interline billing memo for ICH submission
l4_steps.input: Prorated revenue amounts per carrier, tax allocations, coupon status from GDS
l4_steps.output: Billing memo submitted to ICH for each partner carrier within IATA Resolution 743 deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Billing memo submission within T+30 days of travel date per IATA Resolution 743; late filing penalty avoidance rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late coupon status reporting from GDS partners (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport) delays billing cycle — coupon voids and exchanges can arrive up to T+21 days, risking T+30 ICH deadline and triggering IATA Resolution 743 late-filing penalties

l4_steps.name: Validate billing memo against ET coupon at ICH
l4_steps.input: Submitted billing memo, original ET coupon data from issuing carrier, IATA prorate factor tables
l4_steps.output: ICH validation result: accepted billing memo or rejection with error code
l4_steps.kpi: First-pass ICH billing acceptance rate ≥92% of submitted memos
l4_steps.pain_point: Coupon status discrepancies (voided tickets, involuntary reroutes, ADMs already issued) between issuing and validating carrier cause ICH rejections — manual investigation averages 3 hours per rejected memo and ~2.4% of memos are rejected on first pass

l4_steps.name: Issue ADM or ACM to resolve billing discrepancy
l4_steps.system: IATA BSP Link / Amadeus Revenue Accounting (ARA)
l4_steps.input: ICH rejection reason code, original ET data, partner airline's counter-claim if applicable
l4_steps.output: Agent Debit Memo (ADM) or Agent Credit Memo (ACM) issued to partner; revenue amount moved to suspense account pending resolution
l4_steps.kpi: ADM/ACM resolution within 45 days per IATA Resolution 850m; suspense account balance <0.5% of monthly interline revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner carriers frequently contest ADMs citing different prorate factor versions — IATA Interline Dispute and Facilitation System (IDFS) resolution process can extend to 180 days, locking revenue in suspense accounts and distorting monthly revenue reporting

l4_steps.name: Submit net interline settlement to IATA Clearing House
l4_steps.input: Validated billing memos net of ADM/ACM, ICH monthly settlement calendar, partner net positions
l4_steps.output: Net settlement amount per partner airline forwarded to ICH for multilateral netting and disbursement
l4_steps.kpi: ICH settlement submission on-time rate = 100% (ICH settlement runs on fixed monthly calendar with no grace period)
l4_steps.pain_point: Errors in net calculation caused by parallel billing cycles for the same partner (current month billing + prior month ADM adjustments) generate short settlements — ICH charges 1% per month penalty on underpayment and requires supplemental submission

l4_steps.name: Post interline settlement to SAP General Ledger
l4_steps.input: ICH settlement confirmation file with net amounts per partner, tax allocation breakdown
l4_steps.output: Journal entries posted to GL — interline revenue recognition per IFRS 15, accounts receivable/payable updated per partner
l4_steps.kpi: GL posting within T+5 business days of ICH settlement confirmation; period-close accuracy = 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue recognition timing gaps between ARA settlement date and SAP posting cause interline revenue to be recognised in the wrong accounting period — reversals required on average for 3–5% of monthly interline revenue, distorting P&L and requiring CFO sign-off

l4_steps.name: Reconcile prorated actuals against RM interline forecast
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM) + SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO)
l4_steps.input: ICH settlement actuals by partner and route, RM system interline revenue forecast by O&D pair
l4_steps.output: Variance report: actual vs forecast interline yield per route and partner, flagging routes with structural mis-valuation
l4_steps.kpi: Interline yield variance ≤±3% of RM forecast; routes exceeding threshold reviewed within 10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: RM systems optimise for own-metal revenue and treat interline flows as residual — interline revenue attribution to O&D pairs is imprecise, causing systematic undervaluation of interline-dependent routes and suboptimal capacity allocation decisions

l4_steps.name: Audit SPA performance and flag renegotiation triggers
l4_steps.input: 12-month rolling SPA settlement actuals, guaranteed minimum revenue thresholds per SPA, partner traffic volumes
l4_steps.output: SPA performance scorecard per partner; renegotiation recommendation package for routes where guarantees are at risk or partner volumes have shifted >15%
l4_steps.kpi: SPA guarantee achievement rate ≥90% of active agreements; annual SPA review completion by Q1 for all agreements expiring in the calendar year
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated alerting when SPA minimum guarantees are trending below threshold — airlines detect shortfalls only at annual review, by which time the commercial window to renegotiate favourable terms has passed and the partner has already shifted volume to competing carriers
